source.text: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατέ μου τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς νυνὶ ἀπολογίας.

records.literal_gloss: Men brothers and fathers, hear of me the to you now defense.

en.L: "Men, brothers and fathers, hear my defense [which I make] to you now."
en.B: "Brothers and fathers, listen now to the defense I am making before you."
en.R: "My brothers, and you respected older men, please listen to me. I want to answer the charges against me."

fr.L: « Hommes, frères et pères, écoutez la défense que je vous adresse maintenant. »
fr.B: « Frères et pères, écoutez maintenant ce que j’ai à dire devant vous pour ma défense. »
fr.R: « Mes frères, et vous, les hommes âgés que nous respectons, s’il vous plaît, écoutez-moi. Je veux répondre aux accusations portées contre moi. »

es.L: «Hombres, hermanos y padres, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} mi defensa [que hago] ante {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ahora».
es.B: «Hermanos y padres, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} ahora la defensa que {{plural_you:les|os}} presento».
es.R: «Hermanos míos, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hombres mayores a quienes respetamos, {{plural_you:escúchenme|escuchadme}}, por favor. Quiero responder a las acusaciones que hay contra mí».

sw.L: "Wanaume, ndugu na akina baba, sikilizeni utetezi wangu ninaoutoa kwenu sasa."
sw.B: "Ndugu zangu na akina baba, sikilizeni sasa utetezi ninaoutoa mbele yenu."
sw.R: "Ndugu zangu, na ninyi wazee wetu wenye heshima, tafadhali nisikilizeni. Nataka kujibu mashtaka dhidi yangu."

decisions.choice: men, brothers and fathers: a formal, respectful address to the Jewish crowd
alternatives: the men of the crowd only
decisions.reason: Stephen opens his speech before the council with the same words (7:2). Here Paul speaks to the crowd that had run together in the temple courts from the whole city (21:30-36), which need not have been men only. "Brothers" claims kinship with them as fellow Jews. Whether the address takes in the women present cannot be settled from the words.

decisions.choice: fathers: the older, respected men among the hearers
decisions.reason: Living hearers are addressed, as in 7:2, so the word is a title of respect for elders, not a reference to ancestors.

decisions.choice: defense: a reply to charges, as in a court
decisions.reason: The word is used of a legal defense (25:16; 2 Timothy 4:16). The crowd had accused Paul of teaching against the people, the law and the temple (21:28). He answers by telling his own story.

decisions.choice: brothers and fathers, with no inclusive setting; Literal keeps "men, brothers and fathers"
decisions.reason: "Brothers and fathers" is a set pair of address, as in 7:2. An inclusive form of the first word alone would read oddly beside "fathers", so the pair is kept as spoken; the meaning note says that women may have been among the hearers.

decisions.choice: you respected older men; I want to answer the charges against me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title "fathers" and the word "defense" mean here.

decisions.choice: Hombres, hermanos y padres (L); Hermanos y padres (B); Hermanos míos ... hombres mayores (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The formal address to the Jewish crowd (meaning decisions m1, m2), worded as Acts 2:29 and 13:26 word it in Spanish; as in English, it stays without an inclusive setting here.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every word addressed to the crowd
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to the whole crowd, so every second-person plural is the plural_you setting: the ustedes form by default, the vosotros form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: Wanaume, ndugu na akina baba (L); Ndugu zangu na akina baba (B); Ndugu zangu, na ninyi wazee wetu wenye heshima (R)
alternatives: Ndugu zangu na viongozi wa watu wetu (R)
decisions.reason: The same address as Stephen's in 7:2, worded the same at Literal and Balanced. Readable says who the "fathers" are here, the older, respected men in the crowd (meaning decision on fathers), as the English Readable does.

source.text: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ ὅτι τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ προσεφώνει αὐτοῖς μᾶλλον παρέσχον ἡσυχίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard but that in the Hebrew language he was addressing them, more they gave quiet.

en.L: And when they heard that he was addressing them in the Hebrew language, they became all the more quiet.
en.B: When they heard him speaking to them in Hebrew, they grew even quieter.
en.R: The people heard that Paul was speaking to them in Hebrew, their own language. So they became even more quiet.

fr.L: Et quand ils entendirent qu’il leur adressait la parole en langue hébraïque, ils firent d’autant plus silence.
fr.B: Quand ils l’entendirent leur parler en hébreu, le silence devint plus profond encore.
fr.R: Les gens ont entendu que Paul leur parlait en hébreu, leur propre langue. Alors ils ont été encore plus silencieux.

es.L: Y al oír que les hablaba en la lengua hebrea, guardaron aún más silencio.
es.B: Cuando oyeron que les hablaba en hebreo, se quedaron todavía más callados.
es.R: La gente oyó que Pablo les hablaba en hebreo, su propio idioma. Por eso se quedaron aún más callados.

sw.L: Na waliposikia kwamba alikuwa akisema nao kwa lugha ya Kiebrania, wakazidi kunyamaza kimya.
sw.B: Waliposikia akisema nao kwa Kiebrania, wakazidi kunyamaza.
sw.R: Watu walisikia kwamba Paulo alikuwa akisema nao kwa Kiebrania, lugha yao wenyewe. Kwa hiyo wakazidi kunyamaza kimya.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew language: the language of the Jews of the land, most likely Aramaic, possibly Hebrew itself
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in 21:40 and 26:14. In the first century the everyday speech of Jews in Judea was Aramaic, and John uses the related word for Aramaic place names (John 5:2; 19:13). Hebrew was also still in use, so either is possible.

decisions.choice: even more quiet: the hush of 21:40 deepened
alternatives: they kept quiet instead of shouting
decisions.reason: There was already a great silence when he began (21:40). Hearing their own language rather than Greek, they listened even more closely.

decisions.choice: Hebrew, their own language
decisions.reason: Readable says why the language mattered to the crowd.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); the historic present kept at Literal ("il dit", 22:2)
decisions.reason: As in chapter 21 and in John: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative at Literal and Balanced, and Readable uses the passé composé. This holds for the narrative frame of the whole chapter (22:2, 22:22-30); Paul's speech has its own tense (22:3).

decisions.choice: la lengua hebrea (L); hebreo (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Acts 26:14 in Spanish: the Greek says "Hebrew"; meaning decision m1 notes that the spoken language was most likely Aramaic.

source.text: καὶ φησίν·

records.literal_gloss: And he says:

en.L: And he says:
en.B: Then he went on:
en.R: Paul said:

fr.L: Et il dit :
fr.B: Puis il poursuivit :
fr.R: Paul a dit :

es.L: Y dice:
es.B: Luego continuó:
es.R: Pablo dijo:

sw.L: Naye anasema:
sw.B: Kisha akaendelea:
sw.R: Paulo akasema:

decisions.choice: says: a present tense in a past story, making the scene vivid
decisions.reason: Greek storytellers sometimes switch to the present tense at a turning point. The speech that follows is the past event being told.

decisions.choice: went on; said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the whole story in the past tense; Literal shows the Greek present. Readable names Paul.

source.text: Ἐγώ εἰμι ἀνὴρ Ἰουδαῖος, γεγεννημένος ἐν Ταρσῷ τῆς Κιλικίας, ἀνατεθραμμένος δὲ ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ παρὰ τοὺς πόδας Γαμαλιήλ, πεπαιδευμένος κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν τοῦ πατρῴου νόμου, ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τοῦ θεοῦ καθὼς πάντες ὑμεῖς ἐστε σήμερον, ὃς ταύτην τὴν ὁδὸν ἐδίωξα ἄχρι θανάτου, δεσμεύων καὶ παραδιδοὺς εἰς φυλακὰς ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας, ὡς καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς μαρτυρεῖ μοι καὶ πᾶν τὸ πρεσβυτέριον· παρ’ ὧν καὶ ἐπιστολὰς δεξάμενος πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς εἰς Δαμασκὸν ἐπορευόμην ἄξων καὶ τοὺς ἐκεῖσε ὄντας δεδεμένους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἵνα τιμωρηθῶσιν.

records.literal_gloss: I am a man a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, brought up but in the city this at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to [the] strictness of the ancestral law, a zealot being of the God even as all you are today, \v 4 who this the Way persecuted as far as death, binding and handing over to prisons men both and women, \v 5 as also the high priest bears witness to me and all the council of elders; from whom also letters having received to the brothers to Damascus I was going to bring also those there being bound to Jerusalem in order that they might be punished.

en.L: "I am a Jewish man, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, educated according to the strictness of the ancestral law, being zealous for God, just as all of you are today, \v 4 who persecuted this Way to [the] death, binding and handing over to prisons both men and women, \v 5 as the high priest also bears me witness, and all the council of elders. From them I also received letters to the brothers, and I was going to Damascus to bring those who were there also to Jerusalem in chains, so that they might be punished.
en.B: "I am a Jew, born in Tarsus in Cilicia but raised here in this city. I sat at the feet of Gamaliel and was trained with great precision in our ancestral law. I was as zealous for God as every one of you is today. \v 4 I persecuted this Way to the point of death, putting men and women alike in chains and handing them over to prison. \v 5 The high priest himself can confirm this, and so can the whole council of elders. I even got letters from them to our fellow Jews in Damascus, and I set off to bring the people there back to Jerusalem in chains to be punished.
en.R: "I am a Jew. I was born in the city of Tarsus, in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem. I studied under Gamaliel, the teacher of the law. He taught me to keep every detail of the law handed down from our ancestors. I was eager to serve God, just as all of you are today. \v 4 I fought against the people who followed this Way, so hard that some of them died. I arrested men and women and put them in prison. \v 5 The high priest and all the council of elders can tell you that this is true. They gave me letters to our fellow Jews in Damascus. So I went there to arrest the believers and bring them back to Jerusalem in chains to be punished.

fr.L: « Moi, je suis un homme juif, né à Tarse en Cilicie, mais élevé dans cette ville, aux pieds de Gamaliel, instruit selon l’exactitude de la Loi des pères, étant zélé pour Dieu, comme vous l’êtes tous aujourd’hui, \v 4 moi qui ai persécuté cette Voie jusqu’à la mort, liant et livrant aux prisons hommes et femmes, \v 5 comme le grand prêtre aussi m’en rend témoignage, ainsi que tout le conseil des anciens. D’eux j’avais aussi reçu des lettres pour les frères, et je me rendais à Damas pour amener enchaînés à Jérusalem ceux aussi qui étaient là, afin qu’ils soient punis.
fr.B: « Je suis juif. Je suis né à Tarse en Cilicie, mais j’ai été élevé ici, dans cette ville. J’ai été formé aux pieds de Gamaliel, avec une grande rigueur, dans la Loi de nos pères. J’étais aussi zélé pour Dieu que vous l’êtes tous aujourd’hui. \v 4 J’ai persécuté cette Voie jusqu’à la mort, enchaînant hommes et femmes et les livrant à la prison. \v 5 Le grand prêtre lui-même peut le confirmer, ainsi que tout le conseil des anciens. J’avais même obtenu d’eux des lettres pour nos frères juifs de Damas, et je suis parti pour ramener à Jérusalem, enchaînés, ceux qui s’y trouvaient, afin qu’ils soient punis.
fr.R: « Je suis juif. Je suis né dans la ville de Tarse, en Cilicie. Mais j’ai grandi ici, à Jérusalem. J’ai étudié auprès de Gamaliel, le maître de la Loi. Il m’a appris à respecter chaque détail de la Loi que nos ancêtres nous ont transmise. Je voulais de tout mon cœur servir Dieu, comme vous tous aujourd’hui. \v 4 J’ai combattu les gens qui suivaient cette Voie, si durement que certains en sont morts. J’ai arrêté des hommes et des femmes et je les ai mis en prison. \v 5 Le grand prêtre et tout le conseil des anciens peuvent vous dire que c’est vrai. Ils m’ont donné des lettres pour nos frères juifs de Damas. Alors je suis allé là-bas pour arrêter les croyants et les ramener enchaînés à Jérusalem, pour qu’ils soient punis.

es.L: «Yo soy un hombre judío, nacido en Tarso de Cilicia, pero criado en esta ciudad a los pies de Gamaliel, instruido conforme a la exactitud de la ley de [nuestros] padres, siendo celoso de Dios, así como todos {{plural_you:ustedes lo son|vosotros lo sois}} hoy; \v 4 yo perseguí este Camino hasta la muerte, atando y entregando a cárceles tanto a hombres como a mujeres, \v 5 como también el sumo sacerdote me da testimonio, y todo el consejo de ancianos. De ellos también recibí cartas para los hermanos, e iba a Damasco para traer también a los que estaban allí, atados, a Jerusalén, para que fueran castigados.
es.B: «Yo soy judío. Nací en Tarso de Cilicia, pero me crie aquí, en esta ciudad. Me formé a los pies de Gamaliel, y fui instruido con todo rigor en la ley de nuestros antepasados. Era tan celoso de Dios como lo {{plural_you:son todos ustedes|sois todos vosotros}} hoy. \v 4 Perseguí este Camino hasta la muerte: encadenaba a hombres y mujeres por igual y los entregaba a la cárcel. \v 5 El mismo sumo sacerdote puede confirmarlo, y también todo el consejo de ancianos. Incluso recibí de ellos cartas para nuestros hermanos judíos de Damasco, y me puse en camino para traer encadenados a Jerusalén a los que estaban allí, para que fueran castigados.
es.R: «Yo soy judío. Nací en la ciudad de Tarso, en Cilicia. Pero crecí aquí, en Jerusalén. Estudié con Gamaliel, el maestro de la ley. Él me enseñó a cumplir cada detalle de la ley que recibimos de nuestros antepasados. Yo deseaba servir a Dios con todo mi corazón, igual que todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hoy. \v 4 Luché contra la gente que seguía este Camino, con tanta dureza que algunos de ellos murieron. Arrestaba a hombres y a mujeres y los metía en la cárcel. \v 5 El sumo sacerdote y todo el consejo de ancianos pueden {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}} que esto es verdad. Ellos me dieron cartas para nuestros hermanos judíos de Damasco. Así que fui allá para arrestar a los creyentes y traerlos encadenados a Jerusalén para que fueran castigados.

sw.L: "Mimi ni mtu Myahudi, niliyezaliwa Tarso ya Kilikia, lakini nililelewa katika mji huu miguuni pa Gamalieli, nikifundishwa kwa usahihi wote sheria ya baba zetu, nikiwa mwenye juhudi kwa ajili ya Mungu, kama ninyi nyote mlivyo leo; \v 4 mimi niliyeitesa Njia hii hata kufa, nikiwafunga na kuwakabidhi magerezani wanaume kwa wanawake, \v 5 kama kuhani mkuu pia anavyonishuhudia, na baraza lote la wazee; ambao kutoka kwao nilipokea pia barua kwa ndugu, nikaenda Dameski ili kuwaleta Yerusalemu hata wale waliokuwa huko wakiwa wamefungwa, ili waadhibiwe.
sw.B: "Mimi ni Myahudi, niliyezaliwa Tarso huko Kilikia, lakini nililelewa hapa katika mji huu. Nilisoma miguuni pa Gamalieli, nikafundishwa kwa usahihi mkubwa sheria ya baba zetu. Nilikuwa na juhudi kwa ajili ya Mungu kama kila mmoja wenu alivyo leo. \v 4 Niliitesa Njia hii hata kufikia kuua watu, nikiwafunga minyororo wanaume kwa wanawake na kuwakabidhi gerezani. \v 5 Kuhani mkuu mwenyewe anaweza kuthibitisha hilo, na baraza lote la wazee pia. Kutoka kwao nilipokea hata barua kwa ndugu zetu Wayahudi huko Dameski, nikaenda huko ili niwalete watu wa huko Yerusalemu wakiwa wamefungwa minyororo, ili waadhibiwe.
sw.R: "Mimi ni Myahudi. Nilizaliwa katika mji wa Tarso, huko Kilikia. Lakini nilikulia hapa Yerusalemu. Nilisoma chini ya Gamalieli, mwalimu wa sheria. Alinifundisha kushika kila jambo dogo la sheria tuliyopewa na mababu zetu. Nilikuwa na bidii ya kumtumikia Mungu, kama ninyi nyote mlivyo leo. \v 4 Niliwapiga vita watu walioifuata Njia hii, kwa nguvu sana hata baadhi yao wakafa. Niliwakamata wanaume na wanawake, nikawatia gerezani. \v 5 Kuhani mkuu na baraza lote la wazee wanaweza kuwaambia kwamba haya ni kweli. Wao walinipa barua kwa ndugu zetu Wayahudi huko Dameski. Kwa hiyo nilikwenda huko ili kuwakamata waumini na kuwaleta Yerusalemu wakiwa wamefungwa minyororo, ili waadhibiwe.

decisions.choice: at the feet of Gamaliel: as his pupil
decisions.reason: Pupils sat before their teacher, so to sit at someone's feet meant to learn from him (Luke 10:39). Gamaliel was a Pharisee and teacher of the law honored by all the people (5:34).

decisions.choice: at the feet of Gamaliel: goes with "brought up", and the training follows from it
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a comma after the name, so the phrase ends the clause about his upbringing in Jerusalem. Either way, Paul's training under Gamaliel is meant.

decisions.choice: strictness: exact, careful keeping of the law
decisions.reason: The word means exactness. Paul calls the Pharisees "the strictest party of our religion" (26:5).

decisions.choice: zealous for God: wholly devoted to God and his law
alternatives: a member of the Zealot party
decisions.reason: The word is used of devotion to the law in 21:20 and of Paul's earlier life in Galatians 1:14. It does not name the later rebel party here.

decisions.choice: the Way: a name for the followers of Jesus and their teaching
decisions.reason: Luke uses the name in 9:2, 19:9, 19:23, 24:14 and 24:22.

decisions.choice: to the point of death: his persecution went as far as killing
alternatives: until he himself was near death
decisions.reason: Paul says in 26:10 that he cast his vote against believers when they were put to death, and 22:20 recalls Stephen. The phrase does not say how many died.

decisions.choice: council of elders: the Jewish council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same word for the council that tried Jesus (Luke 22:66).

decisions.choice: the high priest bears me witness: the high priest can confirm it
alternatives: the high priest is present now as a witness
decisions.reason: The present tense appeals to the office and its records. The high priest who gave Saul his letters (9:1) need not be the one now in office (23:2).

decisions.choice: the brothers: fellow Jews in Damascus, not believers
decisions.reason: The letters were to the synagogues (9:2). Paul calls his Jewish hearers "brothers" in the same way (22:1; 28:17).

decisions.choice: our fellow Jews
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the brothers were, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: here in Jerusalem; Gamaliel, the teacher of the law; the believers
decisions.reason: Readable names the city, says who Gamaliel was, and says who "those there" were.

decisions.choice: I fought against the people who followed this Way, so hard that some of them died
alternatives: I persecuted this Way to the death
decisions.reason: Readable says what persecuting "to the death" meant, as the meaning note explains. It keeps the number of deaths unstated.

decisions.choice: Paul's account in the passé composé at every level ("j’ai persécuté", "je suis tombé"), with the imperfect for background
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, as in the narrative frame
decisions.reason: Paul is speaking to the crowd, and French tells past events in speech in the passé composé, as the style guide asks for speech. The passé simple would make his defense sound like a written page rather than words spoken from the steps. This holds for the whole speech (22:3-21).

decisions.choice: el consejo de ancianos
decisions.reason: The Greek here is "council of elders" (meaning decision m7), not the word Spanish renders "concilio / Consejo"; lowercase "consejo de ancianos" keeps the two apart while naming the same body.

decisions.choice: nuestros hermanos judíos
decisions.reason: The brothers are fellow Jews, not believers (meaning decision m9); Spanish keeps "hermanos" and adds "judíos", as the English says "fellow Jews".

decisions.choice: ndugu zetu Wayahudi
decisions.reason: The brothers here are fellow Jews in Damascus, not believers (meaning decision on the brothers); Balanced and Readable say so, as the English does. Literal keeps plain "ndugu".

decisions.choice: Njia, with a capital
decisions.reason: "Njia" as a name for the followers of Jesus and their teaching, capitalised as in Acts 9:2.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι πορευομένῳ καὶ ἐγγίζοντι τῇ Δαμασκῷ περὶ μεσημβρίαν ἐξαίφνης ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ περιαστράψαι φῶς ἱκανὸν περὶ ἐμέ, ἔπεσά τε εἰς τὸ ἔδαφος καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι· Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;

records.literal_gloss: It happened but to me journeying and drawing near to Damascus about noon suddenly out of the heaven to flash a light great around me, \v 7 I fell and to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, why me do you persecute?

en.L: And it happened to me, as I was journeying and drawing near to Damascus, about noon, [that] suddenly a great light out of heaven flashed around me. \v 7 And I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'
en.B: As I was traveling and coming close to Damascus, at about midday, all at once a brilliant light from heaven blazed around me. \v 7 I dropped to the ground and heard a voice say to me, 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'
en.R: I was on my way, and I was getting close to Damascus. It was about noon. Suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed all around me. \v 7 I fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice speaking to me. It said, 'Saul, Saul, why are you attacking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'

fr.L: Or, comme j’étais en route et que j’approchais de Damas, vers midi, il m’est arrivé que soudain une grande lumière venue du ciel a brillé autour de moi. \v 7 Je suis tombé sur le sol et j’ai entendu une voix qui me disait : “Saul, Saul, pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} persécutes-tu ?”
fr.B: Comme j’étais en chemin et que j’approchais de Damas, vers midi, une lumière éclatante venue du ciel a soudain resplendi autour de moi. \v 7 Je suis tombé à terre et j’ai entendu une voix me dire : “Saul, Saul, pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} persécutes-tu ?”
fr.R: J’étais en route, et j’arrivais près de Damas. Il était environ midi. Tout à coup, une lumière très forte venue du ciel a brillé tout autour de moi. \v 7 Je suis tombé par terre. Puis j’ai entendu une voix qui me parlait. Elle disait : “Saul, Saul, pourquoi est-ce que tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}attaques ?”

es.L: Y me sucedió que, yendo de camino y acercándome a Damasco, como al mediodía, de repente una gran luz del cielo resplandeció alrededor de mí. \v 7 Y caí al suelo, y oí una voz que me decía: “Saulo, Saulo, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} persigues?”.
es.B: Mientras iba de camino y me acercaba a Damasco, hacia el mediodía, de pronto una luz deslumbrante del cielo brilló a mi alrededor. \v 7 Caí al suelo y oí una voz que me decía: “Saulo, Saulo, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} persigues?”.
es.R: Yo iba de camino, y ya estaba cerca de Damasco. Era como el mediodía. De repente, una luz muy fuerte del cielo brilló a mi alrededor. \v 7 Caí al suelo. Entonces oí una voz que me hablaba. Me decía: “Saulo, Saulo, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} atacas?”.

sw.L: Na ikawa nilipokuwa nikisafiri na kukaribia Dameski, karibu adhuhuri, ghafla nuru kuu kutoka mbinguni ikanimulikia pande zote. \v 7 Nami nikaanguka chini, nikasikia sauti ikiniambia, 'Sauli, Sauli, kwa nini unanitesa?'
sw.B: Nilipokuwa njiani nikikaribia Dameski, yapata saa sita mchana, ghafla nuru kali kutoka mbinguni ilinimulika pande zote. \v 7 Nikaanguka chini, nikasikia sauti ikiniambia, 'Sauli, Sauli, kwa nini unanitesa?'
sw.R: Nilikuwa safarini, nikakaribia Dameski. Ilikuwa yapata saa sita mchana. Ghafla nuru kali kutoka mbinguni ikaangaza pande zote kunizunguka. \v 7 Nikaanguka chini. Kisha nikasikia sauti. Iliniambia, 'Sauli, Sauli, kwa nini unanishambulia?'

decisions.choice: about noon: in full daylight
decisions.reason: The detail is not in 9:3. At midday the sun is at its brightest, yet the light was brighter still (26:13).

decisions.choice: great: very strong, intense
decisions.reason: The word means enough or considerable; with "light" it means a strong, bright light.

decisions.choice: Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me: the same words as in 9:4 and 26:14
decisions.reason: Each telling of the event keeps these words. The doubled name is a solemn call, as when God calls "Abraham, Abraham" (Genesis 22:11).

decisions.choice: attacking
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word for what Saul was doing to the believers.

decisions.choice: persigues (L, B); atacas (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as Acts 9:4 and 26:14 (meaning decision m3), worded as Acts 9:4 is in Spanish at each level.

decisions.choice: Sauli; kutesa (L, B); kushambulia (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as in 9:4: "Sauli" for Saul throughout Acts, and "unanitesa" / "unanishambulia" as there.

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπεκρίθην· Τίς εἶ, κύριε;

records.literal_gloss: I then answered, Who are you, Lord?

en.L: And I answered, 'Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord?'
en.B: 'Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord?' I answered.
en.R: I answered, 'Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord?'

fr.L: Et moi, j’ai répondu : “Qui es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, Seigneur ?”
fr.B: “Qui es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, Seigneur ?” ai-je répondu.
fr.R: J’ai répondu : “Qui es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, Seigneur ?”

es.L: Y yo respondí: “¿Quién eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, Señor?”.
es.B: “¿Quién eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, Señor?”, respondí.
es.R: Yo respondí: “¿Quién eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, Señor?”.

sw.L: Nami nikajibu, 'Wewe ni nani, Bwana?'
sw.B: Nikajibu, 'Bwana, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni nani?'
sw.R: Nikajibu, 'Bwana, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni nani?'

decisions.choice: Lord: a respectful address to the heavenly speaker, whom Saul does not yet know
alternatives: the full confession of Jesus as Lord
decisions.reason: Saul does not know who is speaking, so the word may be only a respectful title. But he has seen a light from heaven, and Luke's readers know who the Lord is. The same question comes in 9:5 and 26:15.

source.text: εἶπέν τε πρὸς ἐμέ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὃν σὺ διώκεις.

records.literal_gloss: He said and to me, I am Jesus the Nazarene whom you persecute.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, 'I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you are persecuting.'
en.B: He told me, 'I am Jesus of Nazareth, the one you are persecuting.'
en.R: He said to me, 'I am Jesus from Nazareth. I am the one you are attacking.'

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a dit : “Je suis Jésus le Nazôréen, que tu persécutes.”
fr.B: Il m’a dit : “Je suis Jésus de Nazareth, celui que tu persécutes.”
fr.R: Il m’a dit : “Je suis Jésus, de Nazareth. C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} que tu attaques.”

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me dijo: “Yo soy Jesús el Nazareno, a quien tú persigues”.
es.B: Él me dijo: “Soy Jesús de Nazaret, el mismo a quien tú persigues”.
es.R: Él me dijo: “Yo soy Jesús de Nazaret. Soy aquel a quien estás atacando”.

sw.L: Naye akaniambia, 'Mimi ni Yesu Mnazareti, ambaye wewe unamtesa.'
sw.B: Akaniambia, 'Mimi ni Yesu wa Nazareti, yule unayemtesa.'
sw.R: Akaniambia, 'Mimi ni Yesu kutoka Nazareti. Mimi ndiye unayenishambulia.'

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: from Nazareth, the name by which Jesus was known
decisions.reason: Peter uses the same name in 2:22 and 3:6. This telling adds it; 9:5 has only "I am Jesus".

decisions.choice: whom you are persecuting: to persecute Jesus's followers is to persecute him
alternatives: Saul had persecuted Jesus in person
decisions.reason: Saul had attacked the believers (22:4), not Jesus himself. The risen Lord counts what is done to his people as done to him.

decisions.choice: of Nazareth; from Nazareth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the name means.

decisions.choice: attacking
decisions.reason: As in 22:7.

source.text: οἱ δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ ὄντες τὸ μὲν φῶς ἐθεάσαντο τὴν δὲ φωνὴν οὐκ ἤκουσαν τοῦ λαλοῦντός μοι.

records.literal_gloss: Those but with me being the indeed light beheld the but voice not heard of the one speaking to me.

en.L: Now those who were with me saw the light, but they did not hear the voice of the one speaking to me.
en.B: My companions saw the light, but they did not hear the voice of the one who was speaking to me.
en.R: The people traveling with me saw the light. But they did not hear the voice of the one who was talking to me.

fr.L: Or ceux qui étaient avec moi ont bien vu la lumière, mais la voix de celui qui me parlait, ils ne l’ont pas entendue.
fr.B: Mes compagnons ont vu la lumière, mais ils n’ont pas entendu la voix de celui qui me parlait.
fr.R: Ceux qui voyageaient avec moi ont vu la lumière. Mais ils n’ont pas entendu la voix de celui qui me parlait.

es.L: Y los que estaban conmigo vieron ciertamente la luz, pero no oyeron la voz del que me hablaba.
es.B: Mis compañeros vieron la luz, pero no oyeron la voz del que me hablaba.
es.R: Las personas que viajaban conmigo vieron la luz. Pero no oyeron la voz del que me estaba hablando.

sw.L: Na wale waliokuwa pamoja nami waliiona ile nuru, lakini hawakuisikia sauti ya yule aliyekuwa akisema nami.
sw.B: Wenzangu waliiona ile nuru, lakini hawakuisikia sauti ya yule aliyekuwa akisema nami.
sw.R: Watu waliosafiri pamoja nami waliiona nuru. Lakini hawakusikia sauti ya yule aliyekuwa akizungumza nami.

decisions.choice: did not hear the voice: the companions did not hear the words spoken to Saul
alternatives: they heard no sound at all
they heard a sound but did not understand it
decisions.reason: In 9:7 the men traveling with Saul stood speechless, "hearing the voice but seeing no one". Here they "saw the light" but "did not hear the voice of the one speaking to me". In 9:7 the word "voice" is in the genitive case after the verb; here it is in the accusative. Some take the difference to mean they heard a sound but did not hear it as words, since the verb can mean to hear with understanding (1 Corinthians 14:2). Others take the two accounts as differing in detail. The case difference does not settle it, since in 22:7 Paul "heard a voice" with the genitive and understood it. Both accounts agree that only Saul received the message.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "saw the light"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("saw indeed the light, and were afraid"), add these words. Others, some of them early, lack them. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: my companions; the people traveling with me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who they were in fewer words.

source.text: εἶπον δέ· Τί ποιήσω, κύριε;

records.literal_gloss: I said then, What shall I do, Lord?

en.L: And I said, 'What shall I do, Lord?'
en.B: I asked, 'What should I do, Lord?'
en.R: I asked, 'Lord, what should I do?'

fr.L: Et j’ai dit : “Que ferai-je, Seigneur ?”
fr.B: J’ai demandé : “Que dois-je faire, Seigneur ?”
fr.R: J’ai demandé : “Seigneur, qu’est-ce que je dois faire ?”

es.L: Y dije: “¿Qué haré, Señor?”.
es.B: Pregunté: “¿Qué debo hacer, Señor?”.
es.R: Pregunté: “Señor, ¿qué debo hacer?”.

sw.L: Nami nikasema, 'Nifanye nini, Bwana?'
sw.B: Nikauliza, 'Nifanye nini, Bwana?'
sw.R: Nikauliza, 'Bwana, nifanye nini?'

decisions.choice: what shall I do: a question that offers obedience
decisions.reason: The form asks what he ought to do. Saul now places himself under the Lord who has spoken to him.

source.text: ὁ δὲ κύριος εἶπεν πρός με· Ἀναστὰς πορεύου εἰς Δαμασκόν, κἀκεῖ σοι λαληθήσεται περὶ πάντων ὧν τέτακταί σοι ποιῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: The and Lord said to me, Having risen go into Damascus, and there to you it will be told about all things which it has been appointed to you to do.

en.L: And the Lord said to me, 'Get up [and] go into Damascus, and there you will be told about everything that has been appointed for you to do.'
en.B: The Lord answered, 'Get up and go on into Damascus. There you will be told all that has been assigned for you to do.'
en.R: The Lord told me, 'Get up and go into Damascus. Someone there will tell you everything God has planned for you to do.'

fr.L: Et le Seigneur m’a dit : “Lève-toi, va à Damas, et là on te parlera de tout ce qu’il t’est prescrit de faire.”
fr.B: Le Seigneur m’a répondu : “Lève-toi et continue jusqu’à Damas. Là, on te dira tout ce que tu as été chargé de faire.”
fr.R: Le Seigneur m’a dit : “Lève-toi et va à Damas. Là-bas, quelqu’un te dira tout ce que Dieu a prévu que tu fasses.”

es.L: Y el Señor me dijo: “Levántate [y] ve a Damasco, y allí se te hablará de todo lo que se te ha asignado hacer”.
es.B: El Señor me respondió: “Levántate y sigue hasta Damasco. Allí se te dirá todo lo que se ha dispuesto que hagas”.
es.R: El Señor me dijo: “Levántate y entra en Damasco. Allí alguien te dirá todo lo que Dios ha planeado que hagas”.

sw.L: Naye Bwana akaniambia, 'Inuka uende Dameski, na huko utaambiwa habari za mambo yote uliyoagizwa kuyafanya.'
sw.B: Bwana akanijibu, 'Inuka, uende mpaka Dameski. Huko utaambiwa yote uliyopangiwa kufanya.'
sw.R: Bwana akaniambia, 'Inuka uende Dameski. Mtu fulani huko atakuambia yote ambayo Mungu amepanga uyafanye.'

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus, who has just named himself
decisions.reason: The speaker is the one who said "I am Jesus" (22:8).

decisions.choice: it will be told; it has been appointed: God is the one who appoints, and someone will tell him
decisions.reason: The passives leave the agents unnamed. The appointing is God's (22:14), and Ananias is the one who tells him (22:12-16).

decisions.choice: someone there will tell you; God has planned
alternatives: it will be told you; it has been appointed
decisions.reason: Readable names who acts, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ὡς δὲ οὐκ ἐνέβλεπον ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τοῦ φωτὸς ἐκείνου, χειραγωγούμενος ὑπὸ τῶν συνόντων μοι ἦλθον εἰς Δαμασκόν.

records.literal_gloss: As but not I was seeing from the glory of the light that, being led by the hand by those being with me I came into Damascus.

en.L: And since I could not see because of the glory of that light, I was led by the hand by those who were with me and came into Damascus.
en.B: Because the glory of that light had left me unable to see, my companions led me by the hand, and I came into Damascus.
en.R: That light was so bright and full of glory that I could not see. So the people with me led me by the hand into Damascus.

fr.L: Et comme je ne voyais plus, à cause de la gloire de cette lumière, conduit par la main par ceux qui étaient avec moi, je suis arrivé à Damas.
fr.B: Comme la gloire de cette lumière m’avait ôté la vue, mes compagnons m’ont pris par la main, et je suis arrivé à Damas.
fr.R: Cette lumière était si forte et si pleine de gloire que je ne voyais plus rien. Alors ceux qui étaient avec moi m’ont conduit par la main jusqu’à Damas.

es.L: Y como no veía a causa de la gloria de aquella luz, llevado de la mano por los que estaban conmigo, llegué a Damasco.
es.B: Como la gloria de aquella luz me había dejado sin vista, mis compañeros me llevaron de la mano, y así llegué a Damasco.
es.R: Aquella luz era tan brillante y tan llena de gloria que yo no podía ver. Por eso los que estaban conmigo me llevaron de la mano hasta Damasco.

sw.L: Na kwa kuwa sikuweza kuona kwa sababu ya utukufu wa nuru ile, niliongozwa kwa mkono na wale waliokuwa pamoja nami, nikaingia Dameski.
sw.B: Utukufu wa nuru ile ulikuwa umeniacha nisiweze kuona, kwa hiyo wenzangu wakaniongoza kwa mkono, nikafika Dameski.
sw.R: Nuru ile ilikuwa kali mno na yenye utukufu, hata sikuweza kuona. Kwa hiyo watu waliokuwa pamoja nami wakanishika mkono, wakaniongoza mpaka Dameski.

decisions.choice: glory: shining splendor
decisions.reason: The word is used of the bright splendor of God's presence (Luke 2:9; Acts 7:55). Here it is the brilliance of the light that blinded him.

decisions.choice: I could not see: a lasting blindness
decisions.reason: The tense describes a state. He was blind for three days (9:9).

decisions.choice: so bright and full of glory
decisions.reason: Readable says what the glory of the light was.

source.text: Ἁνανίας δέ τις ἀνὴρ εὐλαβὴς κατὰ τὸν νόμον μαρτυρούμενος ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν κατοικούντων Ἰουδαίων, ἐλθὼν πρὸς ἐμὲ καὶ ἐπιστὰς εἶπέν μοι· Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ἀνάβλεψον· κἀγὼ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἀνέβλεψα εἰς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Ananias then a certain, a man devout according to the law, borne witness to by all the dwelling [there] Jews, \v 13 having come to me and having stood by said to me, Saul brother, see again; and I in the very hour looked up at him.

en.L: And a certain Ananias, a man devout according to the law, well spoken of by all the Jews living [there], \v 13 came to me, and standing by [me] said to me, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight.' And at that very hour I looked up at him.
en.B: There was a man named Ananias, devout in keeping the law and well regarded by all the Jews who lived there. \v 13 He came and stood beside me and said, 'Brother Saul, see again!' In that very moment my sight came back, and I looked up at him.
en.R: In Damascus there was a man named Ananias. He was a man who honored God and obeyed the law. All the Jews who lived there spoke well of him. \v 13 He came and stood next to me. He said, 'Brother Saul, see again!' Right then I could see again, and I looked at him.

fr.L: Or un certain Ananias, homme pieux selon la Loi, à qui tous les Juifs qui habitaient [là] rendaient un bon témoignage, \v 13 est venu vers moi et, se tenant près [de moi], m’a dit : “Frère Saul, retrouve la vue.” Et moi, à l’heure même, j’ai levé les yeux vers lui.
fr.B: Il y avait un certain Ananias, un homme pieux et fidèle à la Loi, estimé de tous les Juifs qui habitaient là. \v 13 Il est venu se placer à côté de moi et m’a dit : “Saul, mon frère, retrouve la vue !” À l’instant même, j’ai retrouvé la vue et je l’ai regardé.
fr.R: À Damas, il y avait un homme appelé Ananias. Il respectait Dieu et il obéissait à la Loi. Tous les Juifs qui vivaient là disaient du bien de lui. \v 13 Il est venu se mettre à côté de moi. Il m’a dit : “Saul, mon frère, retrouve la vue !” Aussitôt, j’ai pu voir de nouveau, et je l’ai regardé.

es.L: Y un tal Ananías, hombre piadoso según la ley, de quien daban buen testimonio todos los judíos que vivían [allí], \v 13 viniendo a mí y poniéndose a [mi] lado, me dijo: “Hermano Saulo, recobra la vista”. Y yo en esa misma hora alcé la vista hacia él.
es.B: Había un hombre llamado Ananías, piadoso en el cumplimiento de la ley y muy estimado por todos los judíos que vivían allí. \v 13 Vino, se puso a mi lado y me dijo: “¡Hermano Saulo, recobra la vista!”. En ese mismo instante recobré la vista y lo miré.
es.R: En Damasco había un hombre llamado Ananías. Honraba a Dios y obedecía la ley. Todos los judíos que vivían allí hablaban bien de él. \v 13 Vino y se quedó de pie a mi lado. Me dijo: “¡Hermano Saulo, recobra la vista!”. En ese mismo momento pude ver otra vez, y lo miré.

sw.L: Na mtu mmoja, Anania, mtu mcha Mungu kwa kufuata sheria, aliyeshuhudiwa mema na Wayahudi wote waliokaa [huko], \v 13 alinijia, akasimama karibu [nami], akaniambia, 'Ndugu Sauli, upate kuona tena.' Nami saa ile ile nikamtazama juu.
sw.B: Kulikuwa na mtu mmoja aitwaye Anania, mcha Mungu aliyeishika sheria, mwenye sifa njema kwa Wayahudi wote walioishi huko. \v 13 Alinijia, akasimama karibu nami, akasema, 'Ndugu Sauli, ona tena!' Saa ile ile nikapata kuona, nikamtazama.
sw.R: Huko Dameski kulikuwa na mtu aitwaye Anania. Alikuwa mtu aliyemheshimu Mungu na kuitii sheria. Wayahudi wote walioishi huko walimsifu. \v 13 Alikuja, akasimama karibu nami. Akasema, 'Ndugu Sauli, ona tena!' Papo hapo nikaweza kuona tena, nikamtazama.

decisions.choice: devout according to the law: careful to keep God's law
decisions.reason: The word describes reverent, careful people (2:5; 8:2). "According to the law" says how his devotion showed.

decisions.choice: Paul describes Ananias as his hearers would value him: a law-keeping Jew respected by the Jews of Damascus
alternatives: a different Ananias from the one in Acts 9
decisions.reason: In 9:10 Luke calls Ananias a disciple. Speaking to a crowd that accuses him of attacking the law (21:28), Paul stresses that the man who received him was faithful to it. Both descriptions hold.

decisions.choice: receive your sight; I looked up: the same verb, meaning both "see again" and "look up"
decisions.reason: Ananias tells him to see again, and in that hour Saul "looked up" at him: his sight returned, and his first sight was Ananias.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow Jew and now a fellow believer
decisions.reason: Ananias greets Saul as one of his own (9:17).

decisions.choice: see again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plain words; the last clause says both that his sight came back and that he looked at Ananias.

decisions.choice: in Damascus
decisions.reason: Readable says where Ananias lived.

decisions.choice: recobra la vista ... alcé la vista (L); recobré la vista y lo miré (B, R)
decisions.reason: One Greek verb means both "see again" and "look up" (meaning decision m3); Literal repeats "la vista" to keep the echo, and Balanced and Readable say both things the verb does.

decisions.choice: upate kuona tena ... nikamtazama juu (L); ona tena ... nikapata kuona, nikamtazama (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses one verb for "see again" and "look up" (meaning decision on receive your sight); Swahili has no single verb for both, so Literal uses two, and Balanced and Readable say both that his sight came back and that he looked at Ananias, as the English Balanced does.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν προεχειρίσατό σε γνῶναι τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰδεῖν τὸν δίκαιον καὶ ἀκοῦσαι φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἔσῃ μάρτυς αὐτῷ πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὧν ἑώρακας καὶ ἤκουσας.

records.literal_gloss: He and said, The God of the fathers of us appointed you to know the will of him and to see the Righteous One and to hear a voice out of the mouth of him, \v 15 for you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.

en.L: And he said, 'The God of our fathers has appointed you to know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will and to see the Righteous One and to hear a voice from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth, \v 15 for you will be a witness for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to all {{gender:people|men}} of what you have seen and heard.
en.B: Then he said, 'The God of our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} has chosen you beforehand to know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will, to see the Righteous One, and to hear words from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own mouth. \v 15 You will be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} witness to everyone, telling what you have seen and heard.
en.R: Then he said, 'The God our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} worshiped has chosen you. He chose you to know what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants. He chose you to see Jesus, the Righteous One, and to hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} speak to you. \v 15 You will be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} witness to all people. You will tell them what you have seen and heard.

fr.L: Et il a dit : “Le Dieu de nos pères t’a destiné à connaître {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} volonté, à voir le Juste et à entendre une voix venant de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche, \v 15 car tu seras pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} un témoin auprès de {{gender:tous les humains|tous les hommes}} de ce que tu as vu et entendu.
fr.B: Alors il a dit : “Le Dieu de nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} t’a choisi d’avance pour que tu connaisses {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} volonté, que tu voies le Juste et que tu entendes les paroles de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} propre bouche. \v 15 Tu seras {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} témoin devant tout le monde, et tu diras ce que tu as vu et entendu.
fr.R: Puis il a dit : “Le Dieu que nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} adoraient t’a choisi. Il t’a choisi pour que tu connaisses ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} veut. Il t’a choisi pour que tu voies Jésus, le Juste, et que tu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entendes te parler. \v 15 Tu seras {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} témoin devant tout le monde. Tu diras à tous ce que tu as vu et entendu.

es.L: Y él dijo: “El Dios de nuestros padres te ha designado de antemano para conocer {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voluntad, y ver al Justo, y oír una voz de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca, \v 15 porque serás {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} testigo ante {{gender:todas las personas|todos los hombres}} de lo que has visto y oído.
es.B: Entonces me dijo: “El Dios de nuestros {{gender:antepasados|padres}} te ha escogido de antemano para que conozcas {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voluntad, para que veas al Justo y oigas palabras de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia boca. \v 15 Serás {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} testigo ante todo el mundo, y contarás lo que has visto y oído.
es.R: Luego me dijo: “El Dios al que adoraban nuestros {{gender:antepasados|padres}} te ha escogido. Te escogió para que conozcas lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quiere. Te escogió para que veas a Jesús, el Justo, y para que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oigas hablarte. \v 15 Serás {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} testigo ante todas las personas. Les contarás lo que has visto y oído.

sw.L: Naye akasema, 'Mungu wa baba zetu amekuchagua mapema ujue mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na umwone yule Mwenye Haki, na usikie sauti kutoka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, \v 15 kwa kuwa utakuwa shahidi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa watu wote wa mambo uliyoyaona na kuyasikia.
sw.B: Kisha akasema, 'Mungu wa baba zetu amekuchagua tangu mwanzo ili ujue mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, umwone yule Mwenye Haki, na usikie maneno kutoka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. \v 15 Utakuwa shahidi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa watu wote, ukiwaeleza yale uliyoyaona na kuyasikia.
sw.R: Kisha akasema, 'Mungu ambaye mababu zetu walimwabudu amekuchagua. Amekuchagua ujue mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Amekuchagua umwone Yesu, yule Mwenye Haki, na umsikie akisema nawe. \v 15 Utakuwa shahidi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa watu wote. Utawaambia yale uliyoyaona na kuyasikia.

decisions.choice: has appointed: chosen in advance for a task
decisions.reason: The verb means to choose or appoint beforehand (3:20; 26:16).

decisions.choice: our fathers: the forebears of Israel
decisions.reason: Ananias names the God of Israel's forebears, as Peter did in 3:13 and 5:30.

decisions.choice: the Righteous One: a title of Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter (3:14) and Stephen (7:52) use the same title. "His mouth" is the Righteous One's: Saul heard Jesus speak.

decisions.choice: witness: one who tells what he has seen and heard
decisions.reason: As in 1:8 and 26:16, a witness testifies about Jesus from what he knows firsthand.

decisions.choice: all people: all human beings, Gentiles as well as Jews
decisions.reason: The phrase looks ahead to 22:21, where the Lord sends Paul to the Gentiles.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As at 3:13; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: people, with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: Jesus, the Righteous One; He chose you
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus and repeats the verb to keep the sentences short.

decisions.choice: {{gender:antepasados|padres}} (B, R); {{gender:todas las personas|todos los hombres}} (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: the fathers of Israel are the ancestors, and "all people" means all human beings (meaning decisions m2, m5); Literal keeps "padres", and Balanced and Readable say "todo el mundo" and "todas las personas", which need no span.

decisions.choice: baba zetu; watu wote, with no gender span
decisions.reason: "baba zetu" (our forefathers) and "watu wote" (all people) are the plain Swahili for these words; Swahili has no second wording that the gender setting could switch to, so there is no span where the English has one. "Mwenye Haki" for the Righteous One, as in 3:14 and 7:52.

source.text: καὶ νῦν τί μέλλεις;

records.literal_gloss: And now why do you delay?

en.L: And now why are you delaying?
en.B: Now why wait any longer?
en.R: So why wait any longer?

fr.L: Et maintenant, pourquoi tardes-tu ?
fr.B: Maintenant, pourquoi attendre encore ?
fr.R: Alors, pourquoi attendre plus longtemps ?

es.L: Y ahora, ¿por qué te demoras?
es.B: Ahora, ¿por qué esperar más?
es.R: Así que, ¿por qué esperar más?

sw.L: Na sasa kwa nini unakawia?
sw.B: Sasa unangoja nini tena?
sw.R: Basi kwa nini usubiri zaidi?

decisions.choice: why are you delaying: there is no reason to wait
decisions.reason: The question urges him to act at once; Saul had not refused.

source.text: ἀναστὰς βάπτισαι καὶ ἀπόλουσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου ἐπικαλεσάμενος τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Having risen be baptized and wash away the sins of you, having called on the name of him.

en.L: Get up, be baptized and wash away your sins, calling on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.'
en.B: Get up and be baptized. Let your sins be washed away as you call on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.'
en.R: Get up and be baptized. Have your sins washed away as you call on the name of the Lord Jesus.'

fr.L: Lève-toi, fais-toi baptiser et lave-toi de tes péchés, en invoquant {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.”
fr.B: Lève-toi, fais-toi baptiser, et que tes péchés soient lavés, tandis que tu invoques {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.”
fr.R: Lève-toi et fais-toi baptiser. Fais-toi laver de tes péchés en faisant appel au nom du Seigneur Jésus.”

es.L: Levántate, bautízate y lava tus pecados, invocando {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre”.
es.B: Levántate y bautízate, y que tus pecados sean lavados al invocar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre”.
es.R: Levántate y bautízate. Deja que tus pecados sean lavados mientras invocas el nombre del Señor Jesús”.

sw.L: Inuka ubatizwe, na uzioshe dhambi zako, ukiliitia jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.'
sw.B: Inuka ubatizwe. Dhambi zako zioshwe mbali unapoliitia jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.'
sw.R: Inuka ubatizwe. Dhambi zako zioshwe unapoliitia jina la Bwana Yesu.'

decisions.choice: be baptized; wash away: forms that mean "have yourself baptized" and "have your sins washed away"
alternatives: wash away your own sins by your own effort
decisions.reason: Both verbs are in the middle voice: Saul submits to what is done for him. The cleansing is God's work, received as he calls on the Lord.

decisions.choice: baptism, the washing away of sins and calling on his name belong together
alternatives: baptism only follows a forgiveness already complete
decisions.reason: Peter joins baptism with forgiveness in 2:38, and "everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved" in 2:21 (Joel 2:32). The sentence ties the washing to baptism and to calling on the name, without saying which brings about forgiveness.

decisions.choice: his name: the name of the Righteous One, Jesus
decisions.reason: The nearest "he" is the Righteous One (22:14). Believers are those who call on Jesus's name (9:14, 9:21).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "his name"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "the name of the Lord"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("calling on the name of the Lord"), have "the Lord". Others, some of them early, have "his". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the one called on, as the meaning note explains. The pronoun could also be read as God.

decisions.choice: fais-toi baptiser; lave-toi de tes péchés (L), que tes péchés soient lavés (B), fais-toi laver de tes péchés (R)
alternatives: sois baptisé et lave tes péchés
decisions.reason: The Greek forms mean "have yourself baptized" and "have your sins washed away" (m1). French "se faire baptiser" is the everyday way to say this, so every level uses it; "sois baptisé" sounds stiff. Literal keeps a reflexive for the washing as well.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι ὑποστρέψαντι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ προσευχομένου μου ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γενέσθαι με ἐν ἐκστάσει καὶ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν λέγοντά μοι· Σπεῦσον καὶ ἔξελθε ἐν τάχει ἐξ Ἰερουσαλήμ, διότι οὐ παραδέξονταί σου μαρτυρίαν περὶ ἐμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: It happened then to me having returned to Jerusalem and praying of me in the temple to come me into a trance \v 18 and to see him saying to me, Hurry and go out in speed out of Jerusalem, because not they will receive your testimony about me.

en.L: And it happened to me, when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, that I fell into a trance \v 18 and saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saying to me, 'Hurry and go out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not accept your testimony about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'
en.B: After I had come back to Jerusalem, I was praying in the temple when I fell into a trance. \v 18 I saw the Lord, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, 'Hurry! Leave Jerusalem at once, for the people here will not accept what you tell them about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'
en.R: Later I went back to Jerusalem. One day I was praying in the temple, and I fell into a trance. \v 18 I saw the Lord Jesus, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, 'Hurry! Leave Jerusalem right away. The people here will not accept what you say about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

fr.L: Or il m’est arrivé, après mon retour à Jérusalem, alors que je priais dans le temple, de tomber en extase \v 18 et de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voir qui me disait : “Hâte-toi et sors vite de Jérusalem, parce qu’ils n’accepteront pas ton témoignage sur {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.”
fr.B: Après mon retour à Jérusalem, je priais dans le temple quand je suis tombé en extase. \v 18 J’ai vu le Seigneur, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a dit : “Dépêche-toi ! Quitte Jérusalem au plus vite, car les gens d’ici n’accepteront pas ce que tu leur diras de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.”
fr.R: Plus tard, je suis retourné à Jérusalem. Un jour, je priais dans le temple, et je suis tombé en extase. \v 18 J’ai vu le Seigneur Jésus, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a dit : “Dépêche-toi ! Quitte Jérusalem tout de suite. Les gens d’ici n’accepteront pas ce que tu dis sur {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.”

es.L: Y me sucedió que, habiendo vuelto a Jerusalén y estando yo orando en el templo, caí en trance \v 18 y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vi diciéndome: “Apresúrate y sal pronto de Jerusalén, porque no recibirán tu testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}”.
es.B: Después de haber regresado a Jerusalén, estaba orando en el templo cuando caí en trance. \v 18 Vi al Señor, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me dijo: “¡Date prisa! Sal de Jerusalén enseguida, porque la gente de aquí no aceptará lo que les digas acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}”.
es.R: Más tarde volví a Jerusalén. Un día estaba orando en el templo, y caí en trance. \v 18 Vi al Señor Jesús, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me dijo: “¡Date prisa! Sal de Jerusalén enseguida. La gente de aquí no aceptará lo que digas acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}”.

sw.L: Na ikawa niliporudi Yerusalemu, nilipokuwa nikiomba hekaluni, niliingia katika mzubao, \v 18 nikamwona {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akiniambia, 'Fanya haraka, utoke upesi Yerusalemu, kwa sababu hawataupokea ushuhuda wako juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.'
sw.B: Baada ya kurudi Yerusalemu, nilikuwa nikiomba hekaluni, nikazama katika mzubao. \v 18 Nikamwona Bwana, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaniambia, 'Fanya haraka! Ondoka Yerusalemu mara moja, kwa sababu watu wa hapa hawatayakubali yale unayowaambia juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.'
sw.R: Baadaye nilirudi Yerusalemu. Siku moja nilipokuwa nikiomba hekaluni, Mungu alinionyesha maono. \v 18 Nilimwona Bwana Yesu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaniambia, 'Fanya haraka! Ondoka Yerusalemu sasa hivi. Watu wa hapa hawatayakubali yale unayosema juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.'

decisions.choice: trance: a state in which a person sees a vision
decisions.reason: Peter falls into the same state in 10:10 and 11:5.

decisions.choice: a loosely built sentence
decisions.reason: The sentence refers to Paul first with one case, then another, then a third. The meaning is plain.

decisions.choice: praying in the temple: Paul shows his reverence for the temple
decisions.reason: The crowd had accused him of defiling the temple (21:28). This visit is likely his first return after Damascus (9:26-30; Galatians 1:18).

decisions.choice: him: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: The one he sees speaks of testimony "about me", and Paul answers "Lord" (22:19).

decisions.choice: the Lord; the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one Paul saw, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: caí en trance
decisions.reason: The same word as Acts 10:10 and 11:5, where Spanish says "trance" (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: mzubao (L, B); Mungu alinionyesha maono (R)
decisions.reason: As for Peter's trance in 10:10 and 11:5: "mzubao" at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says plainly that God showed him a vision.

source.text: κἀγὼ εἶπον· Κύριε, αὐτοὶ ἐπίστανται ὅτι ἐγὼ ἤμην φυλακίζων καὶ δέρων κατὰ τὰς συναγωγὰς τοὺς πιστεύοντας ἐπὶ σέ·

records.literal_gloss: And I said, Lord, they themselves know that I was imprisoning and beating in each the synagogues those believing on you;

en.L: And I said, 'Lord, they themselves know that I was imprisoning and beating, in synagogue after synagogue, those who believe in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}};
en.B: I answered, 'Lord, these people know well what I did. In one synagogue after another I had those who believe in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} locked up and beaten.
en.R: I answered, 'Lord, these people know what I used to do. I went into the synagogues and found those who believed in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I put them in prison and had them beaten.

fr.L: Et moi, j’ai dit : “Seigneur, ils savent eux-mêmes que moi, je mettais en prison et je battais, dans chaque synagogue, ceux qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ;
fr.B: J’ai répondu : “Seigneur, ces gens savent bien ce que j’ai fait. De synagogue en synagogue, je faisais mettre en prison et battre ceux qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.
fr.R: J’ai répondu : “Seigneur, ces gens savent ce que je faisais avant. J’allais dans les synagogues et je trouvais ceux qui croyaient en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Je les mettais en prison et je les faisais battre.

es.L: Y yo dije: “Señor, ellos mismos saben que yo encarcelaba y azotaba de sinagoga en sinagoga a los que creen en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}};
es.B: Yo respondí: “Señor, esta gente sabe bien lo que hice. En una sinagoga tras otra hacía encarcelar y azotar a los que creen en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}.
es.R: Yo respondí: “Señor, esta gente sabe lo que yo hacía antes. Iba a las sinagogas y buscaba a los que creían en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Los metía en la cárcel y los hacía azotar.

sw.L: Nami nikasema, 'Bwana, wao wenyewe wanajua kwamba mimi nilikuwa nikiwatia gerezani na kuwapiga katika kila sinagogi wale wanaokuamini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}};
sw.B: Nikajibu, 'Bwana, watu hawa wanajua vizuri nilichofanya. Katika sinagogi moja baada ya jingine niliwafunga gerezani na kuwachapa viboko wale wanaokuamini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}.
sw.R: Nikajibu, 'Bwana, watu hawa wanajua nilivyokuwa nikifanya. Nilikwenda katika masinagogi, nikawatafuta wale waliokuamini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}. Niliwatia gerezani na kuwafanya wachapwe viboko.

decisions.choice: Paul's reply: since they know what he once did, his change should persuade them
alternatives: he pleads that he is unworthy
decisions.reason: Paul seems to argue that the people of Jerusalem, who knew him as a persecutor, would have to take note of his turn. The Lord answers by sending him away all the same (22:21).

decisions.choice: beating in the synagogues: punishment by the synagogue authorities
decisions.reason: Synagogues could punish members by flogging (Matthew 10:17). Paul later received such floggings himself (2 Corinthians 11:24).

decisions.choice: those who believe in you: those who trust in Jesus
alternatives: those who agree with his teaching
decisions.reason: The phrase names the believers by their trust in the Lord, as in 9:42 and 11:17.

source.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐξεχύννετο τὸ αἷμα Στεφάνου τοῦ μάρτυρός σου, καὶ αὐτὸς ἤμην ἐφεστὼς καὶ συνευδοκῶν καὶ φυλάσσων τὰ ἱμάτια τῶν ἀναιρούντων αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: and when was being poured out the blood of Stephen the witness of you, also I myself was standing by and approving and guarding the garments of those killing him.

en.L: and when the blood of Stephen, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} witness, was being shed, I myself was also standing by and approving, and guarding the garments of those who were killing him.'
en.B: When Stephen, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} witness, was put to death and his blood poured out, I was there myself. I agreed with what they did, and I looked after the cloaks of those who killed him.'
en.R: Stephen was {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} witness. When they killed him, I was there. I agreed that they should kill him. I even took care of the coats of the men who were killing him.'

fr.L: et quand le sang d’Étienne, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} témoin, était versé, moi aussi j’étais là, approuvant et gardant les vêtements de ceux qui le tuaient.”
fr.B: Quand on a mis à mort Étienne, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} témoin, et que son sang a été versé, j’étais là, moi aussi. J’approuvais ce qu’ils faisaient, et je gardais les manteaux de ceux qui le tuaient.”
fr.R: Étienne était {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} témoin. Quand ils l’ont tué, j’étais là. J’étais d’accord pour qu’ils le tuent. J’ai même gardé les manteaux des hommes qui le tuaient.”

es.L: y cuando se derramaba la sangre de Esteban, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} testigo, yo mismo también estaba presente y [lo] aprobaba, y guardaba los mantos de los que lo mataban”.
es.B: Cuando mataron a Esteban, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} testigo, y se derramó su sangre, yo mismo estaba allí. Estaba de acuerdo con lo que hacían, y cuidaba los mantos de los que lo mataron”.
es.R: Esteban era {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} testigo. Cuando lo mataron, yo estaba allí. Estaba de acuerdo en que lo mataran. Hasta cuidé las capas de los hombres que lo estaban matando”.

sw.L: na damu ya Stefano, shahidi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, ilipokuwa ikimwagwa, mimi mwenyewe pia nilikuwa nimesimama karibu, nikikubaliana [nao], na kuyalinda mavazi ya wale waliokuwa wakimwua.'
sw.B: Stefano, shahidi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, alipouawa na damu yake kumwagwa, mimi mwenyewe nilikuwepo. Nilikubaliana na walichofanya, na nikayalinda mavazi ya nje ya wale waliomwua.'
sw.R: Stefano alikuwa shahidi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}. Walipomwua, nilikuwepo. Nilikubali kwamba wamwue. Hata niliyalinda makoti ya watu waliokuwa wakimwua.'

decisions.choice: witness: one who testified about Jesus, here a witness whose testimony ended in his death
alternatives: martyr, in the later sense of one who dies for the faith
decisions.reason: The word means a witness, as in 1:8 and 22:15. Stephen bore witness to Jesus before the council and was killed for it. The later sense "martyr" grew out of passages like this one and Revelation 2:13, but here the word still means witness.

decisions.choice: Stephen's death: the events of 7:58-8:1
decisions.reason: The witnesses laid their cloaks at Saul's feet (7:58), and Saul approved of the killing (8:1, the same verb as here).

decisions.choice: his blood was poured out: he was violently killed
decisions.reason: Shedding blood means killing (Luke 11:50; Romans 3:15).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "approving"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("consenting unto his death"), add these words, likely from 8:1. Others, some of them early, lack them. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: witness
decisions.reason: The English word "martyr" carries the later sense, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: four short sentences, beginning with Stephen
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence into steps.

decisions.choice: testigo
decisions.reason: Stephen was a witness to Jesus whose testimony ended in his death (meaning decision m1); "mártir" would name only the death, so Spanish keeps "testigo", as the English keeps "witness".

decisions.choice: shahidi
decisions.reason: "shahidi" means a witness and is also the Swahili word for one who dies for the faith, so it carries both senses of the Greek here (meaning decision on witness) without choosing between them.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν πρός με· Πορεύου, ὅτι ἐγὼ εἰς ἔθνη μακρὰν ἐξαποστελῶ σε.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, Go, for I to Gentiles far away will send out you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, 'Go, for I will send you out far away to [the] Gentiles.'"
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told me, 'Go! I am going to send you far away, to the Gentiles.'"
en.R: But the Lord said to me, 'Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles, the people who are not Jews.'"

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a dit : “Va, car moi, je t’enverrai au loin vers les nations.” »
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a dit : “Va ! Je vais t’envoyer au loin, vers les non-Juifs.” »
fr.R: Mais le Seigneur m’a dit : “Va ! Je vais t’envoyer loin d’ici, chez les non-Juifs.” »

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me dijo: “Ve, porque yo te enviaré lejos, a [los] gentiles”».
es.B: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me dijo: “¡Ve! Yo te voy a enviar lejos, a los gentiles”».
es.R: Pero el Señor me dijo: “¡Ve! Te enviaré lejos, a los gentiles, la gente que no es judía”».

sw.L: Naye akaniambia, 'Nenda, kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitakutuma mbali kwa watu wa mataifa.'"
sw.B: Kisha akaniambia, 'Nenda! Mimi nitakutuma mbali, kwa watu wa mataifa.'"
sw.R: Lakini Bwana akaniambia, 'Nenda! Nitakutuma mbali kwa watu wa mataifa, yaani watu wasio Wayahudi.'"

decisions.choice: Gentiles: the peoples who are not Jews
decisions.reason: The word sets the Gentiles against the Jews of Jerusalem who will not accept his testimony (22:18). It is the word that ends his hearing (22:22).

decisions.choice: send out: commission and send, as an apostle
decisions.reason: The verb is built on the same root as "apostle". The commission matches 26:17.

decisions.choice: I: the emphatic "I" of the Lord himself
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out for emphasis: it is the Lord who sends him.

decisions.choice: the Lord; the people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker and says who the Gentiles are.

decisions.choice: chez les non-Juifs (R), with no added explanation
alternatives: chez les non-Juifs, les gens qui ne sont pas juifs
decisions.reason: As at 21:11: "non-Juifs" already says who the Gentiles are, so French Readable does not repeat the explanation English Readable adds.

source.text: Ἤκουον δὲ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι τούτου τοῦ λόγου καὶ ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν λέγοντες· Αἶρε ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς τὸν τοιοῦτον, οὐ γὰρ καθῆκεν αὐτὸν ζῆν.

records.literal_gloss: They were listening then to him until this the word, and they lifted up the voice of them saying, Away from the earth such a one, not for it was fitting him to live.

en.L: And they listened to him until this word, and they raised their voices, saying, "Away with such a [man] from the earth, for it was not fitting [for] him to live!"
en.B: The crowd heard him out until he said this. Then they raised a shout: "Take a man like this off the face of the earth! He should never have been allowed to live!"
en.R: The people listened to Paul until he said this. Then they started shouting, "Kill him! Get rid of him! A man like this should not be allowed to live!"

fr.L: Et ils l’écoutaient jusqu’à cette parole, et ils élevèrent la voix, disant : « Ôte de la terre un tel [homme], car il ne convenait pas qu’il vive ! »
fr.B: La foule l’écouta jusqu’à ces mots. Puis tous élevèrent la voix : « Fais disparaître de la terre un homme pareil ! On n’aurait jamais dû le laisser vivre ! »
fr.R: Les gens ont écouté Paul jusqu’à ce qu’il dise cela. Puis ils se sont mis à crier : « Tuez-le ! Débarrassez-nous de lui ! Un homme comme ça ne devrait pas avoir le droit de vivre ! »

es.L: Y lo escuchaban hasta esta palabra, y alzaron su voz, diciendo: «¡Quita de la tierra a semejante [hombre], porque no convenía que él viviera!».
es.B: La multitud lo escuchó hasta que dijo esto. Entonces se pusieron a gritar: «¡Borra de la faz de la tierra a un hombre así! ¡Nunca debieron dejarlo vivir!».
es.R: La gente escuchó a Pablo hasta que dijo esto. Entonces empezaron a gritar: «¡Que lo maten! ¡Fuera con él! ¡Un hombre así no debe seguir viviendo!».

sw.L: Na walikuwa wakimsikiliza mpaka neno hili, wakapaza sauti zao, wakisema, "Mwondoe [mtu] kama huyu duniani, kwa maana haikufaa yeye kuishi!"
sw.B: Umati ulimsikiliza mpaka aliposema hivyo. Kisha wakapiga kelele, "Mwondoe mtu kama huyu katika uso wa dunia! Hakustahili kuachwa aishi!"
sw.R: Watu walimsikiliza Paulo mpaka aliposema hayo. Kisha wakaanza kupiga kelele, "Auawe! Mwondoe! Mtu kama huyu hastahili kuishi!"

decisions.choice: until this word: until he spoke of being sent to the Gentiles
alternatives: until the end of the speech
decisions.reason: The crowd accepted his story until the Lord sent him to the Gentiles (22:21). That seemed to confirm the charge that he taught against the people (21:28).

decisions.choice: away with such a man from the earth: a cry for his death
alternatives: send him out of the country
decisions.reason: The crowd had shouted "Away with him!" in 21:36, as the crowd shouted about Jesus (Luke 23:18).

decisions.choice: it was not fitting: he ought to have been dead already
decisions.reason: The past tense says it was never right for him to live.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: a past tense, "it was not fitting"
alternatives: many manuscripts have a present form, "it is not fitting"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have a present participle with the same root. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Kill him!
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the crowd wanted, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: κραυγαζόντων τε αὐτῶν καὶ ῥιπτούντων τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ κονιορτὸν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸν ἀέρα, ἐκέλευσεν ὁ χιλίαρχος εἰσάγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν, εἴπας μάστιξιν ἀνετάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιγνῷ δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν οὕτως ἐπεφώνουν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Crying out and them and throwing off the garments and dust throwing into the air, \v 24 ordered the tribune to be brought him into the barracks, having said with whips to be examined him so that he might know for what reason thus they were shouting against him.

en.L: And as they were crying out and throwing off [their] cloaks and throwing dust into the air, \v 24 the tribune ordered him to be brought into the barracks, saying that he should be examined with whips, so that he might find out for what reason they were shouting against him like this.
en.B: They kept yelling, flinging off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air. \v 24 So the tribune ordered Paul taken into the barracks. He gave orders for him to be questioned under the whip, to find out why the people were shouting at him so.
en.R: They kept shouting. They threw off their coats and threw dust into the air. \v 24 So the tribune, the Roman commander, ordered his soldiers to take Paul into the barracks. He told them to whip Paul and question him. He wanted to find out why the people were shouting at Paul like this.

fr.L: Et comme ils criaient, jetaient les manteaux et lançaient de la poussière en l’air, \v 24 le tribun ordonna qu’on le fasse entrer dans la caserne, en disant qu’on l’interroge à coups de fouet, afin qu’il sache pour quelle raison ils criaient ainsi contre lui.
fr.B: Ils continuaient à hurler, à jeter leurs manteaux et à lancer de la poussière en l’air. \v 24 Alors le tribun ordonna de faire entrer Paul dans la caserne et de l’interroger sous le fouet, pour savoir pourquoi le peuple criait ainsi contre lui.
fr.R: Ils continuaient à crier. Ils jetaient leurs manteaux et lançaient de la poussière en l’air. \v 24 Alors le tribun, le commandant romain, a ordonné à ses soldats d’emmener Paul dans la caserne. Il leur a dit de fouetter Paul et de l’interroger. Il voulait savoir pourquoi les gens criaient ainsi contre Paul.

es.L: Y mientras ellos gritaban y arrojaban [sus] mantos y lanzaban polvo al aire, \v 24 el tribuno ordenó que lo metieran en el cuartel, diciendo que lo interrogaran con azotes, para saber por qué causa gritaban así contra él.
es.B: Ellos seguían gritando, arrojando sus mantos y lanzando polvo al aire. \v 24 Entonces el tribuno mandó que llevaran a Pablo al cuartel, y ordenó que lo interrogaran a latigazos para averiguar por qué la gente gritaba así contra él.
es.R: Seguían gritando. Se quitaban las capas y lanzaban polvo al aire. \v 24 Entonces el tribuno, el comandante romano, ordenó a sus soldados que llevaran a Pablo al cuartel. Les dijo que lo azotaran y lo interrogaran. Quería saber por qué la gente le gritaba así a Pablo.

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wakipiga kelele na kutupa mavazi [yao] na kurusha mavumbi hewani, \v 24 kamanda aliamuru aingizwe ndani ya ngome, akisema achunguzwe kwa mijeledi, ili ajue ni kwa sababu gani walikuwa wakimpigia kelele hivyo.
sw.B: Waliendelea kupiga makelele, wakitupa mavazi yao ya nje na kurusha mavumbi hewani. \v 24 Kwa hiyo kamanda aliamuru Paulo aingizwe ndani ya ngome. Akaagiza ahojiwe huku akichapwa mijeledi, ili ajue kwa nini watu walikuwa wakimpigia kelele namna hiyo.
sw.R: Waliendelea kupiga kelele. Walitupa makoti yao na kurusha mavumbi hewani. \v 24 Kwa hiyo kamanda, mkuu wa askari wa Kirumi, akawaamuru askari wake wamwingize Paulo ndani ya ngome. Akawaambia wamchape Paulo mijeledi na kumhoji. Alitaka kujua kwa nini watu walikuwa wakimpigia Paulo kelele namna hiyo.

decisions.choice: throwing off cloaks and throwing dust: signs of rage and horror
alternatives: a sign that they were about to stone him
decisions.reason: Throwing dust was a gesture of anger and contempt (2 Samuel 16:13). Those who stoned Stephen laid aside their cloaks (7:58), so some see a readiness to stone him; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: throwing off: tossing off or waving their cloaks
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw. It can mean to throw off a garment or to toss it about in the air.

decisions.choice: the tribune: the Roman officer in command of the cohort in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The title means a commander of a thousand. He led the Roman garrison in Jerusalem (21:31). His name was Claudius Lysias (23:26).

decisions.choice: the barracks: the soldiers' quarters in the Antonia fortress, beside the temple
alternatives: a military camp outside the city
decisions.reason: The fortress overlooked the temple courts, with steps leading down to them (21:35, 21:40).

decisions.choice: examined with whips: questioned under flogging
decisions.reason: Romans questioned slaves and non-citizens under the whip to force out the truth. The whip was made of leather straps, sometimes weighted with metal or bone.

decisions.choice: Paul; the people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people.

decisions.choice: the Roman commander; his soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says who the tribune was and who carried out his order.

decisions.choice: le tribun; la caserne at every level
decisions.reason: As in chapter 21: "tribun" is the French name of the Roman rank, kept at every level as English keeps "tribune", with Readable saying who he was. "La caserne" follows the English "barracks" here; 21:34 Readable says "la forteresse" where English Readable does.

decisions.choice: el tribuno
decisions.reason: The Roman officer over the cohort in Jerusalem (meaning decision m3), named "tribuno" as in Acts 24:22 and 25:23; Readable adds "el comandante romano" where the English Readable explains the title.

decisions.choice: el cuartel
decisions.reason: The soldiers' quarters in the fortress beside the temple (meaning decision m4); "cuartel" names the place where soldiers live.

decisions.choice: mavazi (L); mavazi ya nje (B); makoti (R)
decisions.reason: The outer cloak, worded as in 9:39 and 22:20.

source.text: ὡς δὲ προέτειναν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἱμᾶσιν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν ἑστῶτα ἑκατόνταρχον ὁ Παῦλος· Εἰ ἄνθρωπον Ῥωμαῖον καὶ ἀκατάκριτον ἔξεστιν ὑμῖν μαστίζειν;

records.literal_gloss: As but they stretched forward him with the straps, said to the standing by centurion the Paul, If a man a Roman and uncondemned it is lawful to you to flog?

en.L: But when they had stretched him out with the straps, Paul said to the centurion standing [there], "Is it lawful for you to flog a man [who is] a Roman and uncondemned?"
en.B: They had stretched him out and tied him with straps when Paul said to the centurion on duty, "Does the law allow you to flog a Roman citizen, and one who has had no trial?"
en.R: The soldiers stretched Paul out and tied him with leather straps. Then Paul spoke to the centurion, the officer standing there. He asked, "Are you allowed to whip a Roman citizen? I have not even been found guilty!"

fr.L: Mais quand ils l’eurent étendu avec les courroies, Paul dit au centurion qui se tenait [là] : « Vous est-il permis de fouetter un homme romain et non condamné ? »
fr.B: Ils l’avaient étendu et attaché avec des courroies quand Paul dit au centurion de service : « Avez-vous le droit de fouetter un citoyen romain, et sans jugement encore ? »
fr.R: Les soldats ont étendu Paul et ils l’ont attaché avec des lanières de cuir. Alors Paul a parlé au centurion, l’officier qui était là. Il lui a demandé : « Est-ce que vous avez le droit de fouetter un citoyen romain ? On ne m’a même pas jugé coupable ! »

es.L: Pero cuando lo estiraron con las correas, Pablo dijo al centurión que estaba presente: «¿Acaso {{plural_you:les|os}} es lícito azotar a un hombre romano y no condenado?».
es.B: Ya lo habían estirado y atado con correas cuando Pablo le dijo al centurión que estaba de guardia: «¿Permite la ley que {{plural_you:ustedes azoten|vosotros azotéis}} a un ciudadano romano, y sin haberlo juzgado?».
es.R: Los soldados estiraron a Pablo y lo ataron con correas de cuero. Entonces Pablo le habló al centurión, el oficial que estaba allí. Le preguntó: «¿{{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} azotar a un ciudadano romano? ¡Ni siquiera me han declarado culpable!».

sw.L: Lakini walipomnyoosha kwa kamba za ngozi, Paulo akamwambia yule akida aliyesimama [pale], "Je, ni halali kwenu kumpiga mijeledi mtu [aliye] Mrumi, naye hajahukumiwa?"
sw.B: Walipokuwa wamekwisha kumnyoosha na kumfunga kwa kamba za ngozi, Paulo alimwambia yule akida aliyesimama pale, "Je, sheria inawaruhusu kumchapa mijeledi raia wa Rumi, tena ambaye hajahukumiwa?"
sw.R: Askari walimnyoosha Paulo na kumfunga kwa kamba za ngozi. Ndipo Paulo akamwambia akida, yule afisa aliyekuwa amesimama pale, "Je, mnaruhusiwa kumchapa mijeledi raia wa Rumi? Hata sijapatikana na hatia!"

decisions.choice: they stretched him out with the straps: they tied him down with leather straps
alternatives: they stretched him out for the lashes of the whip
decisions.reason: The word for straps can mean the thongs that tied a prisoner or the thongs of the whip. Either way he was stretched out, ready to be flogged.

decisions.choice: Roman law forbade flogging a Roman citizen, above all without trial
decisions.reason: Roman laws protected citizens from being flogged, and from being punished without a trial. Paul raised the same point at Philippi (16:37).

decisions.choice: a Roman: a Roman citizen
alternatives: a man from the city of Rome
decisions.reason: In 16:37-38 and here the word means one who has Roman citizenship.

decisions.choice: uncondemned: not tried and found guilty
decisions.reason: The same word is used in 16:37.
