decisions.choice: centurion: a Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers
decisions.reason: He served under the tribune.

decisions.choice: Roman citizen
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "a Roman" means, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: two sentences: a question and a protest
decisions.reason: Readable splits Paul's question in two.

decisions.choice: vous for the Greek plural
alternatives: tu, as Paul says to the tribune in 21:37
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to the centurion, but the Greek "you" is plural: he asks whether the soldiers, all of them, may flog a Roman. French keeps the plural "vous" at every level; it is not a polite "vous" for one man.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:les|os}}, {{plural_you:ustedes azoten|vosotros azotéis}}, {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}}
decisions.reason: Paul's "you" is plural, the centurion and his soldiers, so it is the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: ciudadano romano
decisions.reason: As the English: "a Roman" means a Roman citizen (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Mrumi (L); raia wa Rumi (B, R)
decisions.reason: "a Roman" means a Roman citizen (meaning decision on a Roman); Literal keeps the one word "Mrumi", and Balanced and Readable say "raia wa Rumi", the project's term for a Roman citizen. The same in 22:26-29.

source.text: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης προσελθὼν τῷ χιλιάρχῳ ἀπήγγειλεν λέγων· Τί μέλλεις ποιεῖν;

records.literal_gloss: Having heard then the centurion having gone to the tribune reported saying, What are you about to do?

en.L: And when the centurion heard [this], he went to the tribune and reported [it], saying, "What are you about to do?
en.B: When the centurion heard this, he went to the tribune and told him, "What is this you are about to do?
en.R: When the centurion heard this, he went to the tribune. He said, "Do you know what you are about to do?

fr.L: Et le centurion, l’ayant entendu, alla vers le tribun et fit son rapport en disant : « Qu’es-tu sur le point de faire ?
fr.B: À ces mots, le centurion alla trouver le tribun et lui dit : « Qu’est-ce que tu vas faire là ?
fr.R: Quand le centurion a entendu cela, il est allé voir le tribun. Il lui a dit : « Est-ce que tu sais ce que tu vas faire ?

es.L: Y al oír[lo] el centurión, fue al tribuno y [le] informó, diciendo: «¿Qué vas a hacer?
es.B: Cuando el centurión oyó esto, fue a ver al tribuno y le dijo: «¿Qué es lo que vas a hacer?
es.R: Cuando el centurión oyó esto, fue a hablar con el tribuno. Le dijo: «¿Sabes lo que vas a hacer?

sw.L: Na yule akida aliposikia, alimwendea kamanda, akamwarifu, akisema, "Unataka kufanya nini?
sw.B: Akida aliposikia hayo, alimwendea kamanda, akamwambia, "Unakaribia kufanya nini hiki?
sw.R: Akida aliposikia hayo, alimwendea kamanda, akamwambia, "Je, unajua unachotaka kufanya?

decisions.choice: what are you about to do: a warning in the form of a question
decisions.reason: The centurion warns his commander that he is about to break the law.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "What are you about to do?"
alternatives: many manuscripts add "See" or "Take care" before it
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("Take heed what thou doest"), add a word of warning. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Do you know what you are about to do?
alternatives: What are you about to do?
decisions.reason: Readable makes the warning in the question plain.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: The for man this a Roman is.

en.L: For this man is a Roman."
en.B: This man is a Roman citizen!"
en.R: This man is a Roman citizen!"

fr.L: Car cet homme est romain. »
fr.B: Cet homme est citoyen romain ! »
fr.R: Cet homme est un citoyen romain ! »

es.L: Porque este hombre es romano».
es.B: ¡Este hombre es ciudadano romano!».
es.R: ¡Este hombre es ciudadano romano!».

sw.L: Kwa maana mtu huyu ni Mrumi."
sw.B: Mtu huyu ni raia wa Rumi!"
sw.R: Mtu huyu ni raia wa Rumi!"

decisions.choice: a Roman: a Roman citizen
decisions.reason: As in 22:25.

decisions.choice: Roman citizen
decisions.reason: As in 22:25.

source.text: προσελθὼν δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Λέγε μοι, σὺ Ῥωμαῖος εἶ;

records.literal_gloss: Having come near then the tribune said to him, Tell me, you a Roman are?

en.L: And the tribune came and said to him, "Tell me, are you a Roman?"
en.B: The tribune came over and asked him, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?"
en.R: So the tribune came to Paul and asked, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?"

fr.L: Et le tribun, s’étant approché, lui dit : « Dis-moi, toi, tu es romain ? »
fr.B: Le tribun vint lui demander : « Dis-moi, es-tu citoyen romain ? »
fr.R: Alors le tribun est venu demander à Paul : « Dis-moi, est-ce que tu es citoyen romain ? »

es.L: Y acercándose el tribuno, le dijo: «Dime, ¿tú eres romano?».
es.B: El tribuno se acercó y le preguntó: «Dime, ¿eres tú ciudadano romano?».
es.R: Entonces el tribuno se acercó a Pablo y le preguntó: «Dime, ¿eres ciudadano romano?».

sw.L: Na kamanda akaja, akamwambia, "Niambie, wewe ni Mrumi?"
sw.B: Kamanda akaja, akamwuliza, "Niambie, wewe ni raia wa Rumi?"
sw.R: Kwa hiyo kamanda akamwendea Paulo, akamwuliza, "Niambie, wewe ni raia wa Rumi?"

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, with surprise
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out: the tribune can hardly believe that this prisoner is a citizen.

decisions.choice: Roman citizen
decisions.reason: As in 22:25.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ναί.

records.literal_gloss: He and said, Yes.

en.L: And he said, "Yes."
en.B: "Yes," he said.
en.R: "Yes, I am," Paul answered.

fr.L: Et il dit : « Oui. »
fr.B: « Oui », répondit-il.
fr.R: « Oui, je le suis », a répondu Paul.

es.L: Y él dijo: «Sí».
es.B: «Sí», respondió él.
es.R: «Sí, lo soy», contestó Pablo.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Ndiyo."
sw.B: Akasema, "Ndiyo."
sw.R: Paulo akajibu, "Ndiyo, mimi ni raia."

decisions.choice: he said, Yes: a plain answer
decisions.reason: The tense of the verb is a common one for reporting a reply.

decisions.choice: I am; Paul
decisions.reason: Readable completes the answer and names the speaker.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος· Ἐγὼ πολλοῦ κεφαλαίου τὴν πολιτείαν ταύτην ἐκτησάμην.

records.literal_gloss: Answered then the tribune, I with a great sum the citizenship this acquired.

en.L: And the tribune answered, "I acquired this citizenship for a large sum."
en.B: The tribune replied, "It cost me a great deal of money to get this citizenship."
en.R: "I became a citizen only by paying a large amount of money," the tribune said.

fr.L: Et le tribun répondit : « Moi, c’est pour une grosse somme que j’ai acquis cette citoyenneté. »
fr.B: Le tribun reprit : « Moi, cette citoyenneté m’a coûté beaucoup d’argent. »
fr.R: « Moi, je suis devenu citoyen seulement en payant beaucoup d’argent », a dit le tribun.

es.L: Y respondió el tribuno: «Yo adquirí esta ciudadanía por una gran suma».
es.B: El tribuno replicó: «A mí me costó mucho dinero obtener esta ciudadanía».
es.R: «Yo me hice ciudadano solo después de pagar mucho dinero», dijo el tribuno.

sw.L: Na kamanda akajibu, "Mimi niliupata uraia huu kwa kiasi kikubwa [cha fedha]."
sw.B: Kamanda akajibu, "Mimi ilinigharimu fedha nyingi sana kupata uraia huu."
sw.R: Kamanda akasema, "Mimi nilipata uraia huu kwa kulipa fedha nyingi sana."

decisions.choice: bought citizenship: citizenship obtained by payment
decisions.reason: Under the emperor Claudius citizenship could be obtained for money, often by bribes to officials, as the Roman historian Cassius Dio reports. The tribune's name, Claudius Lysias (23:26), fits a man who took the emperor's name when he became a citizen.

decisions.choice: a large sum: a great amount of money, not stated
decisions.reason: The word means a sum of money. No figure is given, so no modern value can be stated.

decisions.choice: I: emphatic, perhaps doubting that a man like Paul could be a citizen
decisions.reason: The tribune may be suggesting that citizenship is costly and that Paul does not look able to have bought it.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη· Ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ γεγέννημαι.

records.literal_gloss: The but Paul was saying, I but even have been born [so].

en.L: But Paul said, "But I was even born [a citizen]."
en.B: Paul answered, "And I am one by birth."
en.R: Paul answered, "I have been a citizen since I was born."

fr.L: Et Paul dit : « Mais moi, je suis même né [citoyen]. »
fr.B: Paul répondit : « Et moi, je le suis de naissance. »
fr.R: Paul a répondu : « Moi, je suis citoyen depuis ma naissance. »

es.L: Pero Pablo dijo: «Pues yo incluso [lo] soy de nacimiento».
es.B: Pablo respondió: «Y yo lo soy por nacimiento».
es.R: Pablo respondió: «Yo soy ciudadano desde que nací».

sw.L: Lakini Paulo akasema, "Lakini mimi nimezaliwa [raia]."
sw.B: Paulo akajibu, "Lakini mimi ni raia kwa kuzaliwa."
sw.R: Paulo akajibu, "Mimi nimekuwa raia tangu nilipozaliwa."

decisions.choice: born a citizen: his father or an earlier forebear was a Roman citizen
decisions.reason: How Paul's family gained citizenship is not said. One born a citizen held a standing older than the tribune's.

decisions.choice: a citizen; one
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves "citizen" to be understood from the tribune's words.

source.text: εὐθέως οὖν ἀπέστησαν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ οἱ μέλλοντες αὐτὸν ἀνετάζειν· καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος δὲ ἐφοβήθη ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν καὶ ὅτι αὐτὸν ἦν δεδεκώς.

records.literal_gloss: Immediately therefore withdrew from him those being about him to examine; and the tribune also was afraid having learned that a Roman he is and that him he had bound.

en.L: So those who were about to examine him immediately withdrew from him; and the tribune also was afraid, having learned that he was a Roman, and that he had bound him.
en.B: At once the men who were going to question him backed away. The tribune, too, grew afraid once he learned that Paul was a Roman citizen, since he had had him tied up.
en.R: The men who were going to whip and question Paul quickly moved away from him. The tribune was afraid too. He had found out that Paul was a Roman citizen, and he had already had Paul tied up.

fr.L: Aussitôt donc, ceux qui allaient l’interroger s’écartèrent de lui ; et le tribun aussi eut peur, ayant appris qu’il était romain et qu’il l’avait lié.
fr.B: Aussitôt, ceux qui devaient l’interroger reculèrent. Le tribun, lui aussi, prit peur en apprenant que Paul était citoyen romain, car il l’avait fait attacher.
fr.R: Les hommes qui allaient fouetter et interroger Paul se sont vite éloignés de lui. Le tribun aussi a eu peur. Il avait appris que Paul était citoyen romain, et il l’avait déjà fait attacher.

es.L: Así que al instante se apartaron de él los que iban a interrogarlo; y también el tribuno tuvo miedo, al saber que era romano y que lo había atado.
es.B: Al instante se apartaron de él los que iban a interrogarlo. También el tribuno tuvo miedo al enterarse de que Pablo era ciudadano romano, porque lo había hecho atar.
es.R: Los hombres que iban a azotar e interrogar a Pablo se apartaron de él enseguida. El tribuno también tuvo miedo. Se había enterado de que Pablo era ciudadano romano, y ya lo había hecho atar.

sw.L: Basi mara moja wale waliokuwa karibu kumhoji walijitenga naye; na kamanda pia aliogopa, alipotambua kwamba yeye ni Mrumi, na kwamba alikuwa amemfunga.
sw.B: Mara moja wale waliokuwa karibu kumhoji wakajitenga naye. Kamanda naye akaogopa alipotambua kwamba Paulo ni raia wa Rumi, kwa kuwa alikuwa amemfunga.
sw.R: Wale watu waliotaka kumchapa Paulo mijeledi na kumhoji wakaondoka haraka. Kamanda naye akaogopa. Alikuwa amegundua kwamba Paulo ni raia wa Rumi, naye alikuwa tayari amemfunga.

decisions.choice: had bound him: had him tied for flogging, or had him chained
decisions.reason: Paul had been chained since 21:33, and tied with straps for the whip (22:25). To bind a citizen for flogging without trial broke the law. He stays in custody (22:30; 23:10).

decisions.choice: the tribune was afraid: an officer who mistreated a citizen could be punished
decisions.reason: Roman law protected citizens, and an officer who broke it could answer for it.

decisions.choice: examine: question under the whip
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 22:24.

decisions.choice: Paul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Paul.

decisions.choice: whip and question
decisions.reason: Readable says what the examination was, as in 22:24.

source.text: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον βουλόμενος γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς τὸ τί κατηγορεῖται ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἔλυσεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐκέλευσεν συνελθεῖν τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ πᾶν τὸ συνέδριον, καὶ καταγαγὼν τὸν Παῦλον ἔστησεν εἰς αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: On the then next day desiring to know the certain thing, why he is accused by the Jews, he released him and ordered to come together the chief priests and all the council, and having brought down the Paul he set [him] among them.

en.L: And on the next day, wanting to know for certain why he was being accused by the Jews, he released him and ordered the chief priests and all the council to assemble, and he brought Paul down and set [him] before them.
en.B: On the following day, since the tribune wanted to learn the true reason for the charges the Jews were bringing against Paul, he freed him from his chains. He summoned the chief priests and the full council, then brought Paul down and placed him in front of them.
en.R: The next day the tribune wanted to know for sure why the Jews were accusing Paul. So he took off Paul's chains. He ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet together. Then he brought Paul down and had him stand in front of them.

fr.L: Et le lendemain, voulant savoir avec certitude de quoi il était accusé par les Juifs, il le délia et ordonna aux chefs des prêtres et à tout le Sanhédrin de se réunir ; et ayant fait descendre Paul, il le plaça devant eux.
fr.B: Le lendemain, comme le tribun voulait savoir exactement de quoi les Juifs accusaient Paul, il lui fit ôter ses chaînes. Il convoqua les chefs des prêtres et tout le Sanhédrin, puis il fit descendre Paul et le plaça devant eux.
fr.R: Le lendemain, le tribun voulait savoir exactement pourquoi les Juifs accusaient Paul. Alors il a fait enlever les chaînes de Paul. Il a ordonné aux chefs des prêtres et à tout le grand conseil des Juifs de se réunir. Puis il a fait descendre Paul et il l’a fait placer devant eux.

es.L: Y al día siguiente, queriendo saber con certeza por qué era acusado por los judíos, lo soltó, y ordenó que se reunieran los jefes de los sacerdotes y todo el concilio, y haciendo bajar a Pablo, [lo] presentó ante ellos.
es.B: Al día siguiente, como el tribuno quería saber la verdadera razón por la que los judíos acusaban a Pablo, le quitó las cadenas. Convocó a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a todo el Consejo, y luego hizo bajar a Pablo y lo puso delante de ellos.
es.R: Al día siguiente, el tribuno quería saber con seguridad por qué los judíos acusaban a Pablo. Así que le quitó las cadenas. Ordenó que los jefes de los sacerdotes y todo el Consejo Supremo se reunieran. Luego hizo bajar a Pablo y lo puso de pie delante de ellos.

sw.L: Na kesho yake, akitaka kujua hakika kwa nini alikuwa akishtakiwa na Wayahudi, alimfungua, akaamuru wakuu wa makuhani na Baraza Kuu lote wakusanyike, na akiisha kumteremsha Paulo, akamsimamisha mbele yao.
sw.B: Kesho yake kamanda alitaka kujua sababu halisi ya mashtaka ambayo Wayahudi walikuwa wakimletea Paulo. Kwa hiyo akamfungua minyororo, akaamuru wakuu wa makuhani na Baraza Kuu lote wakutane. Kisha akamteremsha Paulo, akamsimamisha mbele yao.
sw.R: Kesho yake kamanda alitaka kujua kwa hakika kwa nini Wayahudi walikuwa wakimshtaki Paulo. Kwa hiyo akamfungua Paulo minyororo. Akaamuru viongozi wa makuhani na Baraza Kuu lote wakutane pamoja. Kisha akamleta Paulo chini, akamsimamisha mbele yao.

decisions.choice: the council: the Sanhedrin, the high council of the Jewish people in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The council was led by the high priest, with chief priests, elders and scribes (4:5-6; 5:21). Paul once had letters from its members (22:5).

decisions.choice: released him: freed him from his chains, while keeping him in custody
decisions.reason: Paul is still the tribune's prisoner (23:10).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "released him"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("loosed him from his bands"), add these words. Others, some of them early, lack them. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: brought down: from the fortress down to where the council met
alternatives: took him to a lower court
decisions.reason: The Antonia fortress stood above the temple courts (21:35).

decisions.choice: the Jews: Paul's Jewish accusers
decisions.reason: The charges came from Jews from Asia and the crowd that followed them (21:27-28).

decisions.choice: the tribune; Paul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people.

decisions.choice: freed him from his chains; took off Paul's chains
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was released, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres; le Sanhédrin (L, B), le grand conseil des Juifs (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles. "Sanhédrin" names the council the meaning note describes (m1); Readable says what it was, where English Readable keeps the plain word "council".

decisions.choice: el concilio (L); el Consejo (B); el Consejo Supremo (R)
decisions.reason: The Jewish high council in Jerusalem (meaning decision m1), named as in Acts 4-5 and 24:20 in Spanish.

decisions.choice: los jefes de los sacerdotes
decisions.reason: As in Acts 25:2, 25:15 and 26:10 in Spanish, at every level.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani (L, B), viongozi wa makuhani (R); Baraza Kuu
decisions.reason: "Baraza Kuu" for the Sanhedrin at every level, as elsewhere in Acts; the chief priests as in the project's Swahili for the Gospels and Acts.
